data.title: Most AI value will come from broad automation, not from R & D
data.author: ydnyshhh
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了人工智能（AI）对未来经济的影响，特别是通过自动化研发（R&D）推动经济增长的观点。尽管一些业内有影响力的人士如Dario Amodei、Demis Hassabis和Sam Altman认为AI将主要通过加速R&D来产生经济效益，文章对此提出质疑。文章指出，R&D对经济增长的实际贡献小于普遍认知，且多数R&D成果无法被企业直接获利。此外，自动化R&D工作的难度高于预期，因为研究工作不仅涉及推理，还需要多种能力。因此，AI的经济价值更可能来自广泛的经济部署，而非仅限于R&D自动化。最终，文章认为AI的广泛应用将推动生产力提升和经济增长，但主要不是通过R&D渠道。

主要讨论点：科技乐观主义与技术进步对社会的影响

不同观点：
• [techpineapple] 认为科技乐观主义令人沮丧，原因有二：一是技术取代人性，二是过度炒作的技术难以实现，缺乏对社会的实际益处。
• [teleforce] 强调约束编程（CP）在解决数据驱动AI无法处理的任务中的潜力，并指出其被忽视的地位以及与AI领域重要人物的历史联系。
• [getnormality] 对文章中关于研发支出与生产力增长关系的论述持怀疑态度，认为其概念抽象且脱离实际。
• [mooreds] 引用一篇2015年的文章，讨论技术部署的重要性，并认为生成型AI仍在探索阶段，而机器学习（ML）已进入部署阶段。
• [bashfulpup] 批评简单与复杂任务自动化的二分法，指出即使简单的任务自动化也面临挑战，并提到RPA（机器人流程自动化）的局限性。
• [mirekrusin] 认为争论研发与一般自动化的受益先后并无意义，指出历史统计数据与当前技术突破的脱节。
• [mitjam] 讨论AI对人力劳动相对价值的影响，提出社会、文化与象征资本的重要性，并预测法规与团体思维可能增加。
• [stego-tech] 将当前自动化趋势比作工业与农业革命，认为广泛的劳动自动化将导致资本提升而非社会提升，除非工人采取行动争取利益分配。
• [KoolKat23] 同意文章观点，认为存在大量低成本高效益的自动化机会，如Excel VBA的普遍使用。
• [yellowapple] 认为AI最终将在经济价值活动中超越人类，但问题在于谁将受益，并提出四种可能的未来情景，从技术乐观主义承诺的乌托邦到反自动化 purges。
• [callamdelaney] 简单计算美国自动化市场的潜在规模，指出10%的工作自动化意味着1.2万亿美元的市场。
• [klooney] 指出美国主要从事研发与服务行业，生产自动化可能不被明显感受到。
• [coldtea] 认为大多数AI自动化将集中在无用的官僚工作上，而非实际生产力提升。
• [AndrewKemendo] 技术上赞同机器将取代人类劳动，尤其是在劳动效率为关键因素的领域，但指出仍未解决“谁将受益”的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于技术进步的实际效益与社会影响，特别是自动化对就业市场与社会结构的冲击。
• 不同评论者对自动化技术成熟度与应用范围的看法存在分歧，一些人认为其潜力被过度炒作，另一些人则看到具体机会与挑战。
• 关于未来社会发展的预测，评论者们提出了多种可能性，从技术乌托邦到反乌托邦，反映了对此技术影响的复杂态度。

43447616.article_content:
A popular view about the future impact of AI on the economy is that it will be primarily mediated through AI automation of R&D. In some form or another, this view has been expressed by many influential figures in the industry:
In his essay
“Machines of Loving Grace”
, Dario Amodei lists five ways in which AI can benefit humanity in a scenario where AI goes well. He considers biology R&D, neuroscience R&D, and economics R&D as three of these ways. There’s no point at which he clearly argues that AI will lead to high rates of economic growth due to being broadly deployed throughout the economy as opposed to speeding up R&D and perhaps improving economic governance.
Demis Hassabis, CEO of DeepMind, is also bullish on R&D as the main channel through which AI will benefit society.
In a recent interview
, he provides specific mechanisms through which this could happen: AI could cure all diseases and “solve energy”. He mentions “radical abundance” as a possibility as well, but beyond the R&D channel doesn’t name any other way in which this could come about.
In his essay
“Three Observations”
, Sam Altman takes a more moderate position and explicitly says that in some ways AI might end up like the transistor, a big discovery that scales well and seeps into every corner of the economy. However, even he singles out the impact of AI on scientific progress as likely to “surpass everything else”.
Overall, this view is surprisingly influential despite not having been supported by any rigorous economic arguments. We’ll argue in this issue that it’s also very likely wrong.
R&D is generally not as economically valuable as people assume – increasing productivity and new technologies are certainly essential for long-run growth, but the contribution of explicit R&D to these processes is smaller than people generally think. Moreover, even most of this contribution is external and not captured in profits by the company performing the R&D, reducing the incentive to deploy systems to perform R&D in the first place. This combination means most AI systems will actually be deployed and earn revenue from tasks that are unrelated to R&D, and in aggregate these tasks will be more economically valuable as well.
It’s also significantly harder to automate R&D jobs than it might naively seem, because most tasks in the job of a researcher are not “reasoning tasks” and depend crucially on capabilities such as agency, multimodality, and long-context coherence. Once AI capabilities are already at a point where the job of a researcher can be entirely automated, it will also be feasible to automate most other jobs in the economy, which for the above reason would most likely create much more economic value than narrowly automating R&D alone.
When we combine these two points, there’s no reason to expect most of the economic value of AI to come from R&D at any point in the future. A much more plausible scenario is that the value of AI will be driven by broad economic deployment, and while we should expect this to
lead to an increase in productivity and output per person
due to increasing returns to scale, most of this increase will probably not come from explicit R&D.

Subscribe
The primary economic impact of AI will be its ability to
broadly
automate labor
There are two related but subtly different claims that we want to tease apart in this section, one we agree with and another we disagree with:
A technology that could automate R&D entirely, and was only used for this purpose, would be highly valuable and would likely add at least a few percentage points to economic growth per year.
We think this claim is true and it’s hard to argue against it.
In the real world, the most socially or economically valuable application of such a technology would in fact be to automate R&D.
This is the claim we will be disputing. While R&D is valuable, we don’t think it’s where we should expect most of the economic value or growth benefits from AI, both before and after AIs exceed human performance on all relevant tasks.
To understand our argument disputing the second claim, we must first measure the actual economic value of R&D. We know that R&D gets its economic value primarily through improving productivity, so to quantify the impact of R&D we might ask how much of the growth in labor productivity in the past has been due to R&D spending and its associated spillovers. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics
estimates that
R&D financed by private firms only accounted for around 0.2%/yr of total factor productivity (TFP) growth in the US from 1988 to 2022, compared to around 0.8%/yr of total TFP growth over the same period and around 1.9%/yr of labor productivity growth.
Though
public R&D spending
is only around a quarter of
total R&D spending
in the US economy, we might also expect it to have larger positive externalities, and

data.title: The Great Hobby Lobby Artifact Heist
data.author: diodorus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Green家族及其企业Hobby Lobby在宗教、文物收购及经营方式等方面的争议和讨论。

不同观点：
• **对作者态度的批评**：
   - [smithkl42] 认为作者在描述Green家族的宗教信仰时过于情绪化，并且带有讽刺口吻。作者应保持中立，不应将个人偏见带入报道。
   - [Beestie] 也提到作者似乎对Green家族不太友好，质疑为何要将故事分为两部分，是否有未揭露的重大问题。
   - [finnthehuman] 同样指出，作者通过贬低读者来引导其观点，这种做法不妥。

• **对文物收购的辩护与质疑**：
   - [wrp] 认为Hobby Lobby在动荡的中东地区购买文物时，面对不确定的来源仍选择自愿接受检查，这是一种在糟糕情况下做正确事的行为。
   - [boomboomsubban] 则批评了破坏木乃伊以寻找隐藏文献的行为，认为这与19世纪将木乃伊磨碎作为万灵药的做法同样恶劣。

• **对Hobby Lobby经营方式的怀疑**：
   - [shaftway] 对Hobby Lobby的定价和库存管理方式表示怀疑，认为其手工录入价格和缺乏条形码系统可能是在为虚假审计或税务减免操作提供便利。
   - [zippyman55] 提到如果将Hobby Lobby店内的“中国制造”产品移除，店铺几乎会空无一物，暗示其产品来源问题。

• **对社区宗教氛围变化的观察**：
   - [flocciput] 观察到Hacker News社区最近似乎变得更加基督教化，出现了更多防御性宗教评论，这与其预期的无神论/不可知论氛围不符。

补充讨论：
• **对故事标题及结构的质疑**：
   - [brightball] 和 [neuroelectron] 都质疑这篇文章为何仍位于网站首页，并指出评论中很多人对故事的意义感到困惑。
   
• **其他相关信息和资源**：
   - [daverol] 提供了BBC播客链接，指出该故事也在其他媒体上被报道。
   - [chiph] 提到Bob Jones大学的宗教艺术收藏，并提供虚拟导览链接。

争议焦点：
• 作者对Green家族宗教信仰的描述方式以及对Hobby Lobby文物收购和经营方式的质疑，是否合理和中立。

data.title: A Brief History of the Miracle Bacterium
data.author: mailyk
data.article_summary:
《奇迹细菌小史》一文介绍了**粘质沙雷氏菌**（*Serratia marcescens*）的科学历史及其对现代科学的影响。这种细菌因其酷似血液的红色外观，常用于研究细菌传播。1904年，英国医生M. H. Gordon在英国议会大厦前进行实验，试图通过议员靴子传播细菌以研究通风系统缺陷，但未成功。随后，他通过在议会厅内漱口并朗诵莎士比亚作品，证明了细菌可通过 speech 传播。

粘质沙雷氏菌最早在1819年因其在玉米粥上形成红色斑点而引起关注，当时被误认为是真菌。尽管其某些菌株对人类有害，但该细菌仍被广泛用于研究微生物传播。文章还提到，随着对其危险性的认识增加，这种细菌逐渐不再用于实验，但仍是生物医学研究的重要对象。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于1969年一篇有关细菌的文章及其历史背景的讨论，特别是与毕达哥拉斯学派和古代哲学相关的趣味内容。

不同观点：
• [dr_dshiv] 分享了一篇1969年的文章，强调了其中关于毕达哥拉斯学派对豆类禁忌的描述，引用了公元170年卢奇安的讽刺作品《出售信条》中的对话，展示了古代哲学与科学的联系。特别指出文章追溯了“血液效应”与毕达哥拉斯学派之间的关系，并以幽默的方式称毕达哥拉斯为“生物学家”。

• [melagonster] 对此表示兴趣，认为内容非常有趣，并表示会尝试寻找更多关于这一类群的信息，显示出对进一步探索和了解相关知识的积极态度。

• [profsummergig] 认为这种科学探究方式是传统的英国做法，并指出类似的实验在今天是 unlikely（不太可能）被允许的。表达了一种对现代科学探究方式的反思，认为现代科学在某些方面失去了过去的一些探索精神。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点可能在于现代科学与传统科学方法的对比上。一方面，传统方法可能包含更多的哲学和文化元素，另一方面，现代科学更强调伦理和实验规范。
• 讨论中还涉及了古代哲学与科学之间的联系，特别是毕达哥拉斯学派的神秘主义与早期科学思维的交织。
• 引用的卢奇安作品为讨论增添了历史和文学的维度，展示了古代对自然现象的解释方式。

At 1:15 p.m. on Monday, August 8th, 1904, a British physician named M. H. Gordon took some soil he had “richly impregnated with a living emulsion” of the virulent bacterium,
1
Serratia marcescens
, and sprinkled it near a lamp post in front of the U.K. House of Commons. Gordon knew that was the exact spot Members of Parliament had to cross before their 2 p.m. session. His hope was for the politicians to step on the contaminated ground and spread the bacteria inside the Debating Chamber.
Gordon wasn’t executing a terrorist attack. Rather, he had been appointed by a committee to study how germs spread inside the House of Commons following an outbreak of influenza among its members. Gordon had chosen
Serratia marcescens
because the bacterium forms easily recognizable red colonies. For his experiment, he placed numerous open Petri dishes inside the Debating Chamber on which the colonies could grow. Gordon’s idea was simple: politicians’ boots would carry contaminated soil and spread
Serratia marcescens
into the building; he would go away with his Petri dishes and reveal colonies of the bacterium to
point at faults
in the House of Commons’ ventilation system.
But despite placing hundreds of Petri dishes around the chamber, Gordon wasn’t able to retrieve more than a handful of colonies. Suspecting the microbe might not spread easily by means of boots, he followed this up with a theatrical experiment: Inside the Debating Chamber, he gargled a suspension of
Serratia marcescens
and recited Shakespeare’s “King Henry V” and “Julius Caesar” for one hour to no one but an audience of open Petri dishes. This time, copious colonies of
Serratia marcescens
appeared, leading him to conclude that speech can transmit microbes as far as 70 feet (21 meters) away.
2
Indeed,
Serratia marcescens’
vivid blood-red color has prompted its use in a wide range of experiments that have increased our understanding of how germs disperse within human bodies, buildings, and populations. Sightings of the striking microbe outside the lab have awakened both fear and awe in the general population.
The awareness that certain strains of
Serratia marcescens
can cause severe harm to humans — counter-intuitively, the paler varieties are most dangerous — only became evident decades after Gordon’s investigations. Before then, hospitals
deliberately sprayed
Serratia marcescens
inside their facilities to investigate microbial dispersion, and laboratory handbooks demonstrated
transmission by handshake
by having students coat their fingers in the microbe. While greater awareness of its dangers eventually led to its discontinuation in tracing experiments,
Serratia marcescens
remains an important subject of biomedical research.
Its scientific journey began over 200 years ago with a bloody polenta.
Subscribe to Asimov Press.
Subscribe
Blood Masquerade
When growing on solid substances, like foodstuffs or Petri dishes filled with agar,
Serratia marcescens
forms red colonies reminiscent of blood, earning it the informal moniker
“masquerader of blood.”
Its appearance on the polenta of a wealthy Paduan farmer during a particularly hot and humid summer in 1819 — ideal conditions for its flourishing — prompted the flurry of investigation that gave it its scientific name.
Serratia marcescens
looks like blood droplets when grown at room temperature on solid media. Mature colonies are mucilaginous, viscous, and tinged bright red or pink with an "
uncanny resemblance
to blood.” Credit:
Benutzer:Brudersohn
After the farmer, Antonio Pittarello, discovered the red-spotted food in his house near Padua, the resultant hubbub of curiosity seekers and the spiritually appalled so disturbed the neighborhood that the local District Commissioner appointed Dr. Vicenze Sette (a physician, surgeon, and district health officer) to investigate the discovery. Also taking an interest in the mysterious “bloody polenta” was
Bartolomeo Bizio
(1791-1862), a young pharmacy student who joined the investigation on his own. In the meantime, red spots started to appear on food in hundreds of homes throughout Pittarello’s village as well as in villages close by.
Through a series of ingenious experiments, Sette and Bizio reproduced the red spots on fresh polenta independently in their own home laboratories. Both concluded (erroneously) that the cause was a microscopic fungus.
3
Sette called it
Zaogalactina imetrofa
(from the Latin, “slime living on food”); Bizio called it
Serratia
4
to honor
43453769.article_summary:
《奇迹细菌小史》一文介绍了**粘质沙雷氏菌**（*Serratia marcescens*）的科学历史及其对现代科学的影响。这种细菌因其酷似血液的红色外观，常用于研究细菌传播。1904年，英国医生M. H. Gordon在英国议会大厦前进行实验，试图通过议员靴子传播细菌以研究通风系统缺陷，但未成功。随后，他通过在议会厅内漱口并朗诵莎士比亚作品，证明了细菌可通过 speech 传播。

粘质沙雷氏菌最早在1819年因其在玉米粥上形成红色斑点而引起关注，当时被误认为是真菌。尽管其某些菌株对人类有害，但该细菌仍被广泛用于研究微生物传播。文章还提到，随着对其危险性的认识增加，这种细菌逐渐不再用于实验，但仍是生物医学研究的重要对象。

data.title: Technicalities of Homeworld 2 Backgrounds
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了经典科幻游戏《家园2》（Homeworld 2）的背景艺术，特别分析了其独特的艺术处理方式。作者和团队对游戏的背景艺术十分钦佩，特别是其草图风格和细节处理。通过使用模组工具提取游戏数据并分析.HOD文件，作者发现背景采用了顶点颜色渐变技术，而非传统贴图。这种方法避免了DDS纹理压缩带来的瑕疵，同时确保背景不会过于抢眼，保持了前后景的清晰区分。文章还提到这种技术在其他游戏如《暗黑3》（Diablo 3）中也有出色表现，并提供了进一步技术分析的参考。最后，文章提到其他开发者如何受《家园》背景艺术的启发应用于个人项目中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《Homeworld》游戏的回忆、技术实现、体验感受以及与其他游戏的比较。

不同观点：
• **怀旧与个人经历**：
  - [moritonal] 提到自己在12岁时曾向父母展示《Homeworld》试玩版，并通过展示精美的导弹图像说服父母购买游戏。
  - [ceejayoz] 回忆1999年看到《Homeworld》beta版的美丽背景，并提到自己多年管理Relic论坛的经历。
  
• **技术实现与开发细节**：
  - [danbolt] 分享了与开发者Aaron Kambietz的交流，指出游戏中使用顶点着色天空盒是为了符合当时的最低配置内存预算，艺术家手工制作了顶点数据，耗时数周。
  - [LarsDu88] 认为如今4k纹理和计算设备普及，这种技术显得有些过时。

• **游戏体验与审美评价**：
  - [tumsfestival] 赞赏《Homeworld》的美丽画面，但也表达了对现实中太空景象不如游戏中美丽的失望，希望更多科幻作品采用类似美学。
  - [egypturnash] 提到早期PS1上的《Spyro the Dragon》游戏也有类似的美丽视觉效果。

• **游戏比较与其他平台的体验**：
  - [nntwozz] 喜欢《Homeworld》系列，但认为《EVE Online》的背景更优越，并分享了一个相关链接。
  - [robin_reala] 提到由于mac 32-bit的淘汰，难以重新运行游戏，并考虑通过Wine等工具尝试。
  - [boppo1] 询问如何在Linux上运行《Homeworld》游戏，以及应该选择原版还是重制版。

• **游戏设计与用户体验**：
  - [anymouse123456] 认为《Homeworld》是少数让人享受且高效的3D交互模型之一，尤其对从事UX或产品设计的人有启发。

• **其他相关内容**：
  - [laurex] 简单表达了对Aaron Kambietz的赞赏，并附上购买艺术书的链接。
  - [retinaros] 询问《Homeworld 3》的表现，表现出对续作的兴趣。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及到《Homeworld》系列的技术细节和视觉美学，以及与其他游戏（如《EVE Online》和《Spyro the Dragon》）的比较。
- 部分评论关注如何在现代系统上运行老游戏，以及对游戏设计和用户体验的评价。
- 争议的焦点并不明显，主要是不同玩家对游戏背景美学的个人偏好和比较。

43452688.article_content:
Russian Version
by
Eliiah
Korean Version
by Woodorl Kim
What you see here
is the stunning background art
of one of the most beautiful sci-fi games.
H o m e w o r l d
2
Thanks for reading.
Just kidding. Of course i have something to say about this. In the company we look at the art of
Homeworld
from time to time and bow to the creators of this masterpiece. Once we talked about how great the background look and how interesting this sketched style is. There is something…some details seem…special to us.
I mentioned, that this looks a bit like… a vertex color gradient. But they wouldn’t paint the background on geometry, right? I mean…that would has to be a highly tessellated sphere.
The discussion was over but I wasn’t satisfied and wanted at least see the textures. So i used some
mod tools
to extract the Homeworld 2 Demo data but there were no textures. Only some .HOD files. I used Google and found a thread how to generate these .HOD files from a .TGA. It was said:
“…scans every pixel of the image then based on contrast
it decides whether or not to add a new vertex and color…”
What?
Could it really be, that this is vertex color? Luckily you can watch at .HOD file with CFHodEdit. And another tool can force a wireframe mode. And now look what this brought to light:
This is one
of the most brave
solution
s for game art
i ever saw.
And here you can see how this influences the sky sphere geometry of the game. Do you see how low the resolution is in the low contrast areas? And how round the sphere is where details were painted?
I never ever had thought, that this can produce such good results. Oh and don’t forget that this technique solves two major problems.
#1
You don’t have any problems with DDS texture compression artifacts.
#2
More important from composition perspective: since you can’t get too fine detail (it was said in the tutorial that the base TGA shouldn’t contain too sharp details), the background stays were it should:
In
the
background
.
Too often i see games where the background contains so much noise and details, that you can’t really separate fore-/midground from background.
The last time i saw this perfect combination of tech & composition was in Diablo 3.
I talk about the 2.5D tree article
.
If you want know more about how these spheres are generated, read
my next article about this topic
.
Thanks for reading.
Update 1
Oskar Stålberg
used the Homeworld-Background-Idea in
his personal project
which looks soooo gorgeous! :,)
Source:
Planet Demo by Oskar Stålberg
Update 2
Chris Correia
works on a space game and asked me about the stars in the Homeworld-Backgrounds because they are super-sharp. I remembered having seen a thread like this a while ago and
here it is
!
In fact, the stars are single textures/billboards:
Source:
Background Star Fields

data.title: A USB Interface to the "Mother of All Demos" Keyset
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: Douglas Engelbart在1960年代初开始探索计算机如何增强人类智力，并开发了许多现代计算的特性，如鼠标、超文本、共享文档、窗口和图形用户界面。在1968年的联合计算机会议上，他通过一场开创性的演示（被称为“所有演示之母”）展示了这些创新。这场演示包括使用一种名为"keyset"的输入设备，但它并未普及。Engelbart的演示还展示了层次文档编辑、图形绘制以及通过远程连接与同事协作，预示了现代计算的许多功能。他的工作受到Vannevar Bush 1945年文章《As We May Think》的启发，旨在增强人类解决复杂问题的能力。Engelbart在斯坦福研究所创立了增强研究中心，并开发了名为NLS的系统，该系统支持交互式文档编辑、代码浏览和数据库检索。这场演示使用了当时先进的硬件和通信技术，连接了Menlo Park和旧金山的会场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕弦键盘（Chorded Keyboard）的历史、应用及其在现代技术中的发展与争议。

不同观点：
• andrehacker认为弦键盘概念有着悠久历史，并提到荷兰80年代的Velotype键盘，该键盘按键更多，学习弦键更容易。他还推荐了《Nerds 2.0.1》这本书和PBS系列作为参考。
• vietjtnguyen讨论了现代自定义机械键盘固件（如QMK和ZMK）中的“组合键”功能，分享了自己使用这些组合键的经验，尤其是在从ZSA Voyager过渡到36键键盘（Chocofi）的过程中，避免使用tap-versus-hold行为，并提供了自己的键盘布局供参考。
• Animats指出最早的弦键盘可以追溯到1897年Baudot的发明，并提供了相关链接，强调这是一个实际部署过的设备，而不仅仅是个原型。
• neilv提到Engelbart的演示中使用的键盘未能流行，但在可穿戴计算领域（如Twiddler）有一定影响。强调弦键盘只需单手操作，并且可以在不需要稳定表面的情况下使用。
• jntun补充了关于Engelbart演示的历史背景，指出演示中的桌子和椅子都是由Herman Miller设计的。
• GregDavidson分享了自己使用Twiddler与Android手机配合的经验，称其可以完全操作桌面计算机上的所有应用，如Emacs。
• imcritic指出相关网站使用了CloudFlare，暗示可能存在安全或隐私问题。
• peteforde提供了关于开关输入去抖动的硬件解决方案建议，推荐使用RC网络和六反相器，而非软件延迟。
• vagab0nd提到在尝试让vim发出不同模式的蜂鸣音时遇到的问题，尤其是无法实现长时间的演示音效。
• jarpineh对弦键盘是否更适合控制计算机、保持良好姿势、避免RSI问题提出了疑问，并讨论了多语言使用者是否能适应弦键盘，是否需要为不同语言优化。
• spit2wind提到了Plover速记引擎，并询问是否有在美国以外制造的速记键盘。

补充讨论：
• DonHopkins提供了关于Doug Engelbart和Valerie Landau合作的详细信息，包括他们在多点触控界面和iPhone上的弦键应用方面的专利，以及他们在推广Engelbart的集体智慧愿景方面的工作。
• 整个讨论中涉及到多个历史背景的补充，如Engelbart的演示视频和他与Landau的合作，丰富了对弦键盘发展和应用的理解。

争议焦点：
• 弦键盘是否适合多语言使用者，是否需要根据语言进行优化设计。
• 关于网站安全和隐私的潜在问题（因使用CloudFlare）。

43453582.article_content:
In the early 1960s, Douglas Engelbart started investigating how computers could augment human intelligence:
"If, in your office, you as an intellectual worker
were supplied with a computer display backed up by a computer that was alive for you all day and was instantly responsive to every
action you had, how much value could you derive from that?"
Engelbart developed many features of modern computing that we now take for granted: the mouse,
1
hypertext, shared documents, windows,
and a graphical user interface.
At the 1968 Joint Computer Conference, Engelbart demonstrated these innovations in a groundbreaking presentation, now known as
"The Mother of All Demos."
The keyset with my prototype USB interface.
Engelbart's demo also featured an input device known as the keyset, but unlike his other innovations, the keyset failed to catch on.
The 5-finger keyset lets you type without moving your hand, entering characters by pressing multiple keys simultaneously as a chord.
Christina Englebart, his daughter, loaned one of Engelbart's keysets to me.
I constructed an interface to connect the keyset to USB, so that it can be used with a modern computer.
The video below shows me typing with the keyset, using the mouse buttons to select upper case and special characters.
2
I wrote this blog post to describe my USB keyset interface.
Along the way, however, I got sidetracked by the history of The Mother of All Demos and how it obtained that name.
It turns out that Engelbart's demo isn't the first demo to be called "The Mother of All Demos".
Engelbart and The Mother of All Demos
Engelbart's work has its roots in
Vannevar Bush's 1945 visionary essay, "
As We May Think
."
Bush envisioned thinking machines, along with the "memex", a compact machine holding a library of collective knowledge with hypertext-style links: "The Encyclopedia Britannica could be reduced to the volume of a matchbox."
The memex could search out information based on associative search, building up a hypertext-like trail of connections.
In the early 1960s, Engelbart was inspired by Bush's essay and set out
to develop means to augment human intellect: "increasing the capability of a man to approach a complex problem situation, to gain comprehension to suit his particular needs, and to derive solutions to problems."
3
Engelbart founded the Augmentation Research Center at the Stanford Research Institute (now SRI), where
he and his team created a system called NLS (oN-Line System).
Engelbart editing a hierarchical shopping list.
In 1968, Engelbart demonstrated NLS to a crowd of two thousand people
at the Fall Joint Computer Conference.
Engelbart gave the demo from the stage, wearing a crisp shirt and tie and a headset microphone.
Engelbart created hierarchical documents, such as the shopping list above, and moved around them with hyperlinks.
He demonstrated how text could be created, moved, and edited with the keyset and mouse.
Other documents included graphics, crude line drawing by today's standards but cutting-edge for the time.
The computer's output was projected onto a giant screen, along with video of Engelbart.
Engelbart using the keyset to edit text. Note that the display doesn't support lowercase text; instead, uppercase is indicated by a line above the character. Adapted from
The Mother of All Demos
.
Engelbart sat at a specially-designed Herman Miller desk
6
that held the
keyset, keyboard, and mouse, shown above.
While Engelbart was on stage in San Francisco,
the SDS 940
4
computer that ran the NLS software was 30 miles to the south in Menlo Park.
5
To the modern eye, the demo resembles a PowerPoint presentation over Zoom, as
Engelbart collaborated with
Jeff Rulifson and Bill Paxton, miles away in Menlo Park.
(Just like a modern Zoom call, the remote connection started with "We're not hearing you. How about now?")
Jeff Rulifson browsed the NLS code, jumping between code files with hyperlinks and expanding subroutines by clicking on them.
NLS was written in custom
high-level languages
, which they developed
with a "compiler compiler" called
TREE-META
.
The NLS system held interactive documentation as well as tracking bugs and changes.
Bill Paxton interactively drew a diagram and then demonstrated how NLS could be used as a database, retrieving information by searching on keywords.
(Although Engelbart was stressed by the live demo, Paxton told me that he was "too young and inexperienced to be concerned.")
Bill Paxton, in Menlo Park, communicating with the conference in San Francisco.
Bill English, an electrical engineer, not only built the first mouse for Engelbart but was also the hardware mastermind behind the demo.
In San Francisco, the screen images were projected on a 20-foot screen by a Volkswagen-sized
Eiodophor projector, bouncing light off a modulated oil film.
Numerous cameras, video switchers and mixers created the video image.
Two leased microwave links and half a dozen antennas connected SRI in Menlo Park to the demo in San Francisco.

43453582.article_summary: Douglas Engelbart在1960年代初开始探索计算机如何增强人类智力，并开发了许多现代计算的特性，如鼠标、超文本、共享文档、窗口和图形用户界面。在1968年的联合计算机会议上，他通过一场开创性的演示（被称为“所有演示之母”）展示了这些创新。这场演示包括使用一种名为"keyset"的输入设备，但它并未普及。Engelbart的演示还展示了层次文档编辑、图形绘制以及通过远程连接与同事协作，预示了现代计算的许多功能。他的工作受到Vannevar Bush 1945年文章《As We May Think》的启发，旨在增强人类解决复杂问题的能力。Engelbart在斯坦福研究所创立了增强研究中心，并开发了名为NLS的系统，该系统支持交互式文档编辑、代码浏览和数据库检索。这场演示使用了当时先进的硬件和通信技术，连接了Menlo Park和旧金山的会场。

data.title: The belay test and the modern American climbing gym
data.author: vasco
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了攀岩天才彼得·梅菲尔德（Peter Mayfield）如何在美国创建首个盈利性室内攀岩馆的故事。20世纪80年代末，攀岩还是一项小众活动，而梅菲尔德在目睹欧洲的攀岩墙后，决心在美国开设类似的设施。他不仅想为专业攀岩者提供训练场所，更希望吸引儿童和企业活动，打造一个“室内攀岩学院”。尽管不被行业看好，梅菲尔德通过在一次攀登中结识投资者，成功筹集资金，并最终实现了他的梦想。他的创新理念改变了攀岩馆的运营模式，为现代攀岩馆的普及奠定了基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：攀岩馆文化、安全检查（belay test）的必要性、攀岩行业的历史与发展、技术与创新对攀岩的影响

不同观点：
• **关于belay test的争议**：
   - **mordechai9000**：认为belay test是必要的，因为即使是经验丰富的攀岩者也会在安全检查中失误，导致事故。举例说明一些老手因 complacency 而犯错，如国际运动员的教练在使用grigri时因分心导致攀爬者坠落。
   - **marsten**：回忆起90年代攀岩馆的早期发展，提到一些有经验的攀岩者如Peter在室内和户外攀岩中都非常出色，且belay test在当时并不普遍。

• **现代攀岩馆的便利性**：
   - **drcode**：提到现代攀岩馆使用autobelay设备，使得独自一人也可以安全攀爬，同时强调初学者仍需上课并通过belay test。
   - **dgfitz**：分享了一次因belayer失误而导致自己对绳索攀爬失去信任的经历，从此转向抱石攀岩。

• **攀岩行业的保守性与创新挑战**：

• **攀岩馆的历史和发展**：
   - **packetlost**：分享了其家族在90年代参与攀岩馆创业的历史，特别是在威斯康星州经营"The Barn"的经历，最终促成了Boulders Climbing Gym的成立。
   - **necubi**：提到Berkeley Ironworks的历史演变，指出其从City Rock继承而来，并与现代攀岩馆对比，认为其虽然老旧但仍有魅力。

• **个人攀岩经历与技术发展**：
   - **egl2020**：分享了自己在1970年通过belay test的经历，使用混凝土块和hip belay方法。

补充讨论：

• **belay test的必要性**：一些评论者认为belay test对于确保安全至关重要，而另一些评论者则通过个人经历指出即使通过测试的人也可能犯错，导致对绳索攀爬失去信心。

Peter Mayfield bouldering at City Rock
Photo: Peter Mayfield Collection

Forty years ago, there was not a single purpose-built climbing gym in the U.S. In 1987, Seattle’s Vertical Club opened and a year later, the Portland Rock Gym launched. But the concept of a profitable indoor climbing gym was far from proven. This is the story of the person whose vision and determination would revolutionize climbing gyms as we know them today.
Peter Mayfield was a climbing prodigy. At 16 years old, in 1978, he was repeating the hardest free climbs in Yosemite. He went on to establish some of the hardest aid routes on the Valley’s big walls. By the age of 19, he was guiding for the prestigious Yosemite Mountaineering School, and became chief guide a year later. When sport climbing competitions began in the late 1980s, Mayfield participated in the first ever Snowbird climbing competition as well as Jeff Lowe’s national competitions.
In 1988, Mayfield formed a guiding cooperative with legends Kim Schmitz and
Jim Bridwell
, but by his mid-twenties, he was looking for a job that would keep him closer to home. So when Bridwell returned from a trip to Europe with posters and magazines of climbing walls going up in France, Mayfield knew he’d found his next venture.
Peter Mayfield at 19 years old on his first ascent in 1981 of Zenyatta Mondatta on El Cap with Jim Bridwell. Twenty years after his FA, Mayfield repeated the route with his 19-year-old son Braden. (Photo: Peter Mayfield Collection)
At the time, the walls in France were closer to artwork in public spaces than purpose-built climbing structures. It was around that time that the Vertical Club—a space for experienced climbers to train—went up, but Mayfield had something completely different in mind. As chief guide of the Yosemite Mountaineering School, he didn’t just want to create a place for himself and his buddies to get stronger. “I had this serious career of turning people onto this sport,” reflects Mayfield. “I was really thinking [about] kids, corporate programs … The word gym wasn’t even in my mind. It was more like an indoor climbing institute.”
With the popularity of
indoor climbing gyms
these days, it’s hard to imagine what it was like in the late ’80s, when climbing itself was still very much a niche activity. Mayfield knew that to keep the gym lights on, he’d need to attract more than just his hardcore climbing buddies.
Then there was the problem with California’s legendary great weather. Mayfield was skeptical that climbers would want to climb indoors on days when the sun was shining, because unlike Seattle and Portland, you could climb outdoors virtually year-round. So his marketing plan was also designed to get non-climbers to come to his gym. He wanted to build a place where “10,000 eight-year-old girls could try something they never dreamed of.”
“That was my pitch,” Mayfield says.
The economics of the first commercial climbing gym
Mayfield found his first investor while guiding an ascent of
Alaska’s Moose’s Tooth
. Tent-bound by storms for days, he discussed his climbing gym dreams with his clients. At the end of the expedition, as they were splitting up at the Oakland Airport, one of the clients asked him what he needed to start his business. He replied that he needed money for a phone line. The client pulled out his wallet and gave him $200. “I literally got handed two C-notes to start my business,” he remembers. He used that money to put in a Pacific Bell phone line in his mother’s basement in Berkeley and got to work.
“I got no positive reaction from the [climbing] industry at all,” remembers Mayfield. “I was pretty connected because I climbed with Bridwell. I met with the CEO of The North Face. I met with the CEO of Marmot. I met with the president of REI. They all said ‘it will never work. It makes sense in Seattle where it rains. Who would ever climb indoors in California?”
Mayfield even sent his business plan to Yvon Chouinard. “He was very polite and gave me some good advice,” Mayfield recalls. “He did not invest. None of them invested. But he kind of got what I was talking about.” (Chouinard did tell Mayfield that he should try to sell milkshakes: “If you can nail it with the youth, you will kick ass.”)
So Mayfield widened his net, contacting ”everybody in Silicon Valley who had ever climbed” and raised half a million dollars with 48 limited partners, essentially a large group of $5,000 investors. He stalled for a while, dealing with the mountain of paperwork associated with creating such a high volume of limited partnerships. But in the midst of his fundraising, he produced the Great Outdoor Adventure Fair in San Francisco. To promote his concept to the general public, he set up a portable climbing wall at the fair. data.title: Supply Chain Attacks on Linux Distributions – Fedora Pagure
data.author: akyuu
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了针对Linux发行版Fedora的Pagure基础设施的供应链攻击。作者Thomas Chauchefoin指出，攻击者利用了Pagure代码托管平台的漏洞，植入了恶意代码，可能影响众多依赖该平台的开发项目。攻击主要通过伪造的提交和未经授权的访问进行，威胁到软件构建过程的完整性。文章建议开发者加强安全措施，如启用双因素认证、定期审计代码变更，并使用签名验证来确保代码来源的可靠性。Fedora团队正在积极修复漏洞并提升系统安全性，以防止类似攻击再次发生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bash的bashrc行为、Linux供应链安全、SSH和Git配置问题、开源社区的信任问题

不同观点：
• [blueflow] 认为Bash在通过sshd启动时加载bashrc是不合理的设计，尤其当bashrc向stdout写数据时会导致git和rsync无法工作。这种特殊情况需要通过在bashrc中添加条件判断来避免。
• [lrvick] 提出Linux供应链安全存在问题，并介绍了一个名为[Stageˣ]的替代方案。该方案具有确定性、可重现性，并且从极小的可审计机器代码启动，所有发布的内容都经过多方审查和签名，强调了对现有发行版信任单一维护者的担忧。
• [guillem_lefait] 提到在法国网络安全播客中，作者们在两周内发现Fedora和openSUSE的漏洞，表明选择最弱路径可以快速找到攻击向量。
• [cadamsdotcom] 认为像xz/lzma漏洞这样的问题可能是由少数合谋的人引入的，尤其是在开放源代码社区中对匿名贡献者的过度信任可能导致安全隐患。在macOS上使用Homebrew和oh-my-zsh时也会有类似担忧。
• [superb_dev] 指出Git可以通过设置login shell为`git-shell`来解决SSH连接问题，可能适用于某些自定义配置。
• [ufo] 对Git需要使用`--end-of-options`表示不满，认为这种做法不合理。
• [INTPenis] 分享了自己尝试向Fedora贡献包时遇到需要赞助者的问题，最终放弃。
• [bbarnett] 提到界面标题覆盖屏幕的问题，但与主要讨论主题关系不大。
• [TZubiri] 认为使用Red Hat产品而不从Red Hat获取可能导致风险，暗指节省成本可能带来安全隐患。

补充讨论：
• Bash的bashrc行为被认为是潜在的安全风险，尤其是在远程连接和自动化任务中。
• 开源社区中对维护者和贡献者的信任问题引发了对供应链安全的广泛担忧。
• 不同的技术解决方案被提出以解决特定问题，如Git的shell配置和Bash的bashrc处理。
• 讨论中还涉及了开放源代码社区中潜在的合谋风险和安全漏洞的发现方法。

• [lrvick] 提出Linux供应链安全存在问题，并介绍了一个名为[Stageˣ]的替代方案。该方案具有确定性、可重现性，并且从极小的可审计机器代码启动，所有发布的内容都经过多方审查和签名，强调了对现有发行版信任单一维护者的担忧。
• [guillem_lefait] 提到在法国网络安全播客中，作者们在两周内发现Fedora和openSUSE的漏洞，表明选择最弱路径可以快速找到攻击向量。
• [cadamsdotcom] 认为像xz/lzma漏洞这样的问题可能是由少数合谋的人引入的，尤其是在开放源代码社区中对匿名贡献者的过度信任可能导致安全隐患。在macOS上使用Homebrew和oh-my-zsh时也会有类似担忧。
• [superb_dev] 指出Git可以通过设置login shell为`git-shell`来解决SSH连接问题，可能适用于某些自定义配置。
• [ufo] 对Git需要使用`--end-of-options`表示不满，认为这种做法不合理。
• [INTPenis] 分享了自己尝试向Fedora贡献包时遇到需要赞助者的问题，最终放弃。
• [bbarnett] 提到界面标题覆盖屏幕的问题，但与主要讨论主题关系不大。
• [TZubiri] 认为使用Red Hat产品而不从Red Hat获取可能导致风险，暗指节省成本可能带来安全隐患。

补充讨论：
• Bash的bashrc行为被认为是潜在的安全风险，尤其是在远程连接和自动化任务中。
• 开源社区中对维护者和贡献者的信任问题引发了对供应链安全的广泛担忧。
• 不同的技术解决方案被提出以解决特定问题，如Git的shell配置和Bash的bashrc处理。
• 讨论中还涉及了开放源代码社区中潜在的合谋风险和安全漏洞的发现方法。

data.title: Aiter: AI Tensor Engine for ROCm
data.author: hochmartinez
data.article_summary: AMD推出了AI Tensor Engine for ROCm (AITER)，这是一个高性能AI运算符的集中存储库，旨在加速各种AI工作负载。AITER提供了一个统一的平台，方便用户将优化后的运算符集成到私有、公共或自定义框架中。其关键特性包括多功能、易用的设计，支持C++和Python（Torch API）双编程接口，强大的内核基础设施，以及全面的内核支持（包括推理工作负载、训练内核、GEMM操作和通信内核）。AITER还支持定制和优化内核环境，并与AMD ROCm无缝集成，从而最大化GPU性能。通过AITER的优化，用户可以在多种AI操作中获得显著的性能提升，例如GEMM性能提升2倍，Mixture of Experts (MoE)操作性能提升3倍等。在vLLM/SGLang中集成AITER后，DeepSeek模型的吞吐量提升了超过2倍。

AITER: AI Tensor Engine For ROCm
Contents
AITER: AI Tensor Engine For ROCm
#
March 21, 2025 by
Shekhar Pandey
,
Liz Li
, Carlus Huang, Lingpeng Jin,
Anshul Gupta
.
5 min read. | 1331 total words.
Software tools & optimizations
AI/ML
Performance optimization is critical when working with GPUs, especially for tasks involving artificial intelligence, which can be extremely demanding. To fully leverage the capabilities of advanced hardware, it’s essential to master optimization strategies and ensure every available resource is utilized efficiently. In this blog we will provide an overview of AMD’s AI Tensor Engine for ROCm (AITER) and show you how easy it is to integrate AITER kernels in basic LLM training and inference workload. AITER helps developers to focus on creating operators while allowing customers to seamlessly integrate this operator collection into their own private, public, or any custom framework.
What is AI Tensor Engine for ROCm (AITER)
#
AMD is introducing the AI Tensor Engine for ROCm (AITER), a centralized repository filled with high-performance AI operators
[
1
]
designed to accelerate various AI workloads. AITER serves as a unified platform where customers can easily find and integrate optimized operators into their existing frameworks—be it private, public, or custom-built as you can see in Figure 1 below. With AITER, AMD simplifies the complexity of optimization, enabling users to maximize performance while providing flexibility to meet diverse AI requirements.
Figure 1: Block level diagram of AITER
#
Key Features
#
Versatile and User-Friendly Design:
AITER’s architecture is carefully crafted for versatility and ease of use, allowing seamless integration into various workflows and systems.
Dual Programming Interfaces:
At the highest abstraction level, AITER supports two primary interfaces—C++ and Python (Torch API). This dual-interface approach makes AITER highly accessible, catering to developers with different programming preferences and skillsets.
Robust Kernel Infrastructure:
Underneath the user-level APIs, AITER employs a powerful and robust kernel infrastructure. This infrastructure is built upon a variety of underlying technologies, including Triton, CK (Compute Kernel), ASM (Assembly), and HIP (Heterogeneous Interface for Portability).
Comprehensive Kernel Support:
The AITER kernel ecosystem efficiently supports diverse computational tasks such as inference workloads, training kernels, GEMM (General Matrix Multiplication) operations, and communication kernels. Such comprehensive kernel support ensures that users can confidently handle complex and resource-intensive AI tasks.
Customizable and Optimizable Kernel Ecosystem:
With its rich kernel environment, AITER allows developers to perform customized optimizations tailored specifically to their applications. This flexibility helps developers to bypass or overcome architectural limitations, resulting in significantly enhanced performance and adaptability.
Seamless Integration with AMD ROCm:
At its core, AITER leverages AMD’s ROCm, ensuring efficient bridging between optimized kernels and AMD GPUs. This integration unlocks the full potential and peak performance of AMD GPUs, delivering optimal efficiency across a wide range of AI workloads.
By combining user-friendly interfaces, extensive kernel capabilities, and robust GPU integration, AITER empowers developers to achieve maximum efficiency and performance in their AI applications.
Performance Gains with AITER
#
By leveraging AITER’s advanced optimizations, users can experience significant performance improvements across various AI operations:
AITER block-scale GEMM:
Achieves up to
2x performance boost
[
2
]
, substantially accelerating general matrix multiplication tasks.
AITER block-scale fused MoE:
Delivers up to
3x performance boost
[
3
]
, optimizing the efficiency of Mixture of Experts (MoE) operations.
AITER MLA for decode:
Provides an impressive
up to 17x performance boost
[
4
]
, dramatically enhancing decoding efficiency.
AITER MHA for prefill:
Realizes up to
14x performance boost
[
5
]
, significantly improving Multi-Head Attention (MHA) performance during prefill stages.
AITER’s Integration in vLLM/SGLang for DeepSeek V3/R1
#
The integration of AITER into vLLM/SGLang for the DeepSeek v3/r1 model has led to remarkable improvements in total token throughput (tokens per second, tok/s). Before AITER’s integration, the throughput stood at
6484.76 tok/s
. After incorporating AITER’s optimizations, throughput dramatically increased to
13704.36 tok/s
, marking more than a
2x improvement
[
6
]
in processing speed as shown in Figure 2 below.

43451968.article_summary: AMD推出了AI Tensor Engine for ROCm (AITER)，这是一个高性能AI运算符的集中存储库，旨在加速各种AI工作负载。AITER提供了一个统一的平台，方便用户将优化后的运算符集成到私有、公共或自定义框架中。其关键特性包括多功能、易用的设计，支持C++和Python（Torch API）双编程接口，强大的内核基础设施，以及全面的内核支持（包括推理工作负载、训练内核、GEMM操作和通信内核）。AITER还支持定制和优化内核环境，并与AMD ROCm无缝集成，从而最大化GPU性能。通过AITER的优化，用户可以在多种AI操作中获得显著的性能提升，例如GEMM性能提升2倍，Mixture of Experts (MoE)操作性能提升3倍等。在vLLM/SGLang中集成AITER后，DeepSeek模型的吞吐量提升了超过2倍。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在天气预测中的应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [rkagerer] 提出是否所有历史数据（如浮标、气象气球、气象站等）以及过去的天气模型预测都已被存储，以便AI算法可以在历史数据上运行并与现有方法进行性能对比。他还提到了是否存在一个集中的数据中心来存储这些数据。
• [eternityforest] 则关注AI是否能够通过普通消费级传感器或诸如摄像头、麦克风阵列等设备来进行本地天气预报。
• [jedberg] 指出，用于收集数据的资金被削减，这可能会影响数据的获取和天气预报的准确性，并提供了一篇相关文章的链接。
• [lenerdenator] 对模型的准确性提出了挑战，特别是在堪萨斯城地铁的天气预测中，两天以上的预测准确性较差。
• [timthorn] 提供了Richard Turner的一次演讲链接，讨论了AI天气预测的工作原理。
• [MostlyStable] 提出了一个假设，即未来的AGI代理是否能够像人类本能地预测球的飞行轨迹一样，本能地进行天气预测。
• [kgwgk] 提供了相关论文的链接。
• [herodoturtle] 提到了一个旧的FogCreek实习项目，并回忆了一部相关的纪录片。
• [bazzargh] 讨论了Turing Institute的历史，并提到过去的AI研究与现在的不同。
• [politelemon] 对模型如何取代数据收集步骤提出了疑问。
• [westoque] 提到其父亲在海洋微风和降雨模型方面的研究，并表示对AI和机器学习在天气预测中的进展感兴趣。
• [noiv] 提供了模型数据的链接。
• [dsr_] 指出文章中并未明确说明新模型的准确性是否能与当前最佳模型相媲美。
• [abdullahkhalids] 质疑在气候快速变化的背景下，过去的经验不再能预测未来，ML模型的鲁棒性如何。
• [interludead] 对模型如何处理飓风或罕见的极端天气事件等边缘情况表示关注。

补充讨论：
• 数据存储与访问：多个评论提到了历史数据存储和访问的重要性，包括是否存在一个集中的数据中心。
• 模型的准确性与性能对比：讨论了新AI模型与现有模型的性能对比，以及在不同天气情况下的预测准确性。
• 资金与资源问题：提到资金削减对数据收集和天气预报准确性的影响。
• 未来AI的发展：探讨了未来AGI代理在天气预测中的潜力及其与人类预测方式的类比。
• 极端天气事件的处理：对模型在处理罕见天气事件方面的能力表示关注。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于一个展示物种活体首次已知照片的项目更新。项目目前有超过7,000个观察记录和2,000名成员。文章重申了项目规则：1) 提交的照片必须是该物种在全球范围内的首次照片，而不仅限于iNaturalist；2) 必须是活体照片，标本、死物等不符合条件；3) 如果物种有性别二型或不同生命阶段，各阶段的照片可以分别提交。文章还感谢了成员的贡献，特别是用户@borisb在甲虫类照片上的大量工作。项目已基本自给自足，每日有用户添加新记录。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于iNaturalist项目“首次已知物种照片”的定义和其意义的讨论

不同观点：
• [rex_lupi] 认为该项目的目标是收集世界上任何物种的首次已知照片，无论是否提交到iNaturalist。这些照片必须是公开发表或分享过的，并且包括未描述物种的首次照片记录，或已描述但不常见的物种的首次照片记录。如果发现项目中的照片并非该物种的首张照片，应告知项目创建者以便移除。历史照片也欢迎，只要是自己拍摄的。

• [madpen] 对iNaturalist及其Seek应用表示赞赏，认为其有助于自然探索和学习，但也提到ChatGPT在物种识别方面有时表现更好，表明技术进步对传统自然观察工具的潜在影响。

• [shabadoo75] 提到项目创建者发表了一篇关于该项目在物种监测和保护方面重要价值的论文，强调了项目的科学贡献。

• [nxpnsv] 和 [4ugSWklu] 表达了对项目中某些稀有物种（如仅被观察一次的虫子或未被拍摄到的Crump’s Mouse）的兴趣和期待。

• [Tewboo] 对能看到生物的最早图像表示极为 fascination，认为这是科学史上的突破性时刻。

• [a3w] 和 [bobsmooth] 对项目是否包含人类照片提出疑问，[bobsmooth] 明确指出项目中没有人类照片。

• [Nition] 认为项目概念很酷，但对其实际内容（主要是2020年代的照片而非1800年代的照片）感到失望，并提供了一个1860年代家猫首张照片的例子以作对比。

补充讨论：
• 项目创建者rex_lupi强调了照片的历史性和首次公开发表的要求。
• 部分评论者如[madpen]关注iNaturalist与现代技术（如ChatGPT）的关系。
• [shabadoo75] 通过引用学术论文强调了项目的科学价值。
• [Nition] 的评论引发了对项目期望与实际内容不符的争议，期望看到更老的历史照片。

争议焦点：项目是否应包含更老的历史照片，而非仅限于现代照片，这影响了用户对项目的期望和体验。

To my great surprise, I just realised it's been more than two and a half years since I last wrote a journal post for this project! Very lax of me, and apologies to all for the lack of more regular updates.
The project has been surging along, and we now have more than 7,000 observations, which is fantastic to see. We also recently surpassed 2,000 project members, thanks in part to some regular mentions of the project in recent iNat blog posts (eg observation of the week).
So for all the newer members, I'll run through the project rules again:
1 . Any observations you add must be the first photograph(s) of that species anywhere. If an observation is the first one for that species to be uploaded to iNat, but other photos of that species from an earlier point in time already exist anywhere elsewhere online/in print, then that observation should not be added to the project. This is the biggest source of observations that I have to remove from the project. So your observation must be both the first photograph of that species on iNat and also the first anywhere.
If you encounter an observation of a species that is older than one already in the project, add it, but please message me so I can remove the one that no longer qualifies as oldest.
2 . Your photograph must be of a living individual. A number of observations have been added that depict things like empty mollusc shells, dead fishes, pinned insects, etc. Whilst these are of course valuable observations, they are not eligible for the project.
3 . If the male and female of a species are sexually dimorphic, then both are valid to be added to the project. So too if a species has distinct life stages (eg caterpillar/chrysalis/butterfly), they are all valid to be separately added to the project (assuming the other rules apply). Ditto for plants; if one observation shows the first ever photos of flowers, and another the first ever of fruits, they are both ok to add to the project. Please make sure, however, that the first two rules are also followed in these cases.
The project is very much self-sustaining now, with users adding observations to it every day, and there are a number of users in particular who have added many IDs and/or added records to the project, so huge thanks to everyone involved. I'd like to especially highlight the recent efforts of
@borisb
, who has contributed tremendously (IDing and adding) in the world of beetles and has been a very vocal advocate for the project, letting users know each time he adds one of their observations.

data.article_summary: "Shift-To-Middle Array" 是一种创新的动态数组结构，旨在优化两端的插入和删除操作，同时保持连续内存存储，提高缓存局部性和并行处理效率。其特点包括均摊 O(1) 的两端插入和删除、O(1) 随机访问、优于链表的缓存局部性、支持SIMD和并行优化以及更高效的内存使用。与 std::deque 和链表相比，它在多项操作上具有更好的时间复杂度。该项目提供了 C++ 和 Java 版本的基准测试和示例代码，适用于高性能队列、游戏引擎、实时应用和网络数据处理等场景。项目采用 MIT 许可证，欢迎贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Shift-To-Middle Array数据结构的实现、性能及其与现有数据结构（如std::deque、环形缓冲区、Boost::devector等）的比较。

不同观点：
• **ksherlock**：指出C++实现中非平凡类型（如std::unique_ptr）可能引发的问题，建议添加static_assert确保类型是可平凡复制的。同时提出front()应返回引用，并建议添加迭代器以兼容算法库。
• **pizlonator**：提到JavaScriptCore使用类似技术处理JavaScript数组，并提供了相关代码链接，认为这种技术性能不错但实现难度较高。
• **AttilaT**：介绍Shift-To-Middle Array的设计目标和优点，如双端插入删除的高效性、缓存利用率、随机访问性能等，并提供了性能基准测试结果，主张在某些高性能场景下使用。
• **rwbt**：指出Apple的CoreFoundation CFArray和NSMutableArray也使用了类似技术，并提供了相关资源链接。
• **pcwalton**：提出使用mmap实现循环缓冲区的想法，指出其优势和缺点（如重新分配缓慢和最小数组大小限制）。
• **dzaima**：批评ExpandingRingBuffer.h使用取模运算进行索引计算，认为这是低效的，并建议使用按位与操作以提升性能。
• **TylerGlaiel**：指出该数据结构在特定操作下可能会无限增长，即使元素数量保持较小。
• **bogdan-lab**：认为稳定内存属性是deque的重要特性，建议直接使用vector并通过旋转实现类似功能，而不是像该实现那样操作原始内存，认为其复杂且易错。
• **kragen**：对描述感到困惑，尝试将其与gap buffer或环形缓冲区进行类比，并询问其与ExpandingRingBuffer的区别。
• **jeffzha**：询问该实现与Boost::devector的比较。
• **orlp**：分享了自己类似的未完成项目经验，并详细描述了一种避免过度复制的策略，主张不总是将元素移到中间，而是在需要时动态增长和调整。
• **delifue**：指出在特定操作模式下，该实现可能比环形缓冲区的deque涉及更多复制，从而性能更差。
• **alextingle**：调侃描述文本特意称其为deque的替代品，但复杂性比较中却没有与deque对比。
• **kistaro**：质疑该实现是否与Apple SDK中的NSMutableArray重复。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Shift-To-Middle Array的实现复杂性、性能优势及其与现有数据结构的实际比较。
• 不同实现策略（如元素移动到中间、使用环形缓冲区、动态增长策略等）在不同场景下的优劣。
• 关于稳定内存属性的重要性和如何有效实现的讨论。

Shift-To-Middle Array
The
Shift-To-Middle Array
is a dynamic array designed to optimize
insertions and deletions at both ends
, offering a high-performance alternative to
std::deque
,
std::vector
, and linked lists. It achieves this while maintaining
contiguous memory storage
, improving
cache locality
and enabling
efficient parallel processing
.
🌟 Features
✅
Amortized O(1) insertions & deletions at both ends
✅
Fast random access (O(1))
✅
Better cache locality than linked lists
✅
Supports SIMD & parallel optimizations
✅
Efficient memory usage compared to
std::deque
📌 How It Works
Unlike
std::deque
, which uses a fragmented block structure, the
Shift-To-Middle Array
dynamically
redistributes space
to avoid costly shifts. When resizing, elements are moved toward the middle, ensuring
efficient insertions at both ends
without excessive copying.

🏆 Performance Benchmarks
Benchmarks comparing
Shift-To-Middle Array vs.
std::deque
vs. ExpandingRingBuffer vs.
std::queue
demonstrate that performance improvements depend on
CPU and GPU capabilities
, such as
multi-core parallelism, SIMD optimizations, and cache efficiency
.
The benchmarks were compiled using
GCC with the
-O3
optimization flag
, ensuring high-performance execution. Results vary based on
hardware specifications
and
workload characteristics
.
📂 Installation & Usage
To use Shift-To-Middle Array in your project:

🔬 When To Use
High-performance queue structures
Game engines & real-time applications
Networking (packet buffering, event queues)
Dynamic sequences in computational geometry & physics

Running Java Benchmarks

Java benchmarks

Full API reference and benchmarks are available in the
Wiki
!
📊 Benchmarks & Results
For full benchmark details, check out the
benchmarks report
. The provided
Python scripts
can be used to visualize performance metrics from CSV benchmark results.
🏛 History
The
Shift-To-Middle Array
was developed as part of an effort to create a more efficient
implementation strategy for lists and deques
. Traditional data structures, such as
std::deque
and linked lists, suffer from
poor cache locality
or
fragmented memory allocations
, leading to inefficiencies. By leveraging
contiguous memory
, dynamic mid-shifting, and modern CPU optimizations, Shift-To-Middle Array provides a
balanced solution
for insertion, deletion, and access performance.

data.title: LangManus: An Open-Source Manus Agent with LangChain + LangGraph
data.author: gfortaine
data.article_summary:
LangManus是一个由社区驱动的AI自动化框架，基于开源社区的工作，目标是结合语言模型与专用工具，如网页搜索、爬虫和Python代码执行，同时回馈社区。该项目旨在进行学术研究，参与GAIA排行榜，并计划发表相关论文。它独立于开发者的本职工作，与任何公司或组织无关，并采用MIT许可证开源。

LangManus使用多代理系统架构，包含监督器和规划器等代理，以协调完成复杂任务。例如，自动计算HuggingFace上DeepSeek R1的影响指数，通过在线搜索、数据抓取和Python计算，最终生成报告。

项目提供详细的使用指南，包括克隆仓库、安装依赖、配置环境和运行项目的步骤。贡献和问题将在开发者的业余时间处理，可能会有延迟。使用该项目需自行承担风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LangManus项目的介绍与反馈，包括对项目名称的建议、功能评价以及用户需求。

不同观点：
• [SweetSoftPillow] 指出"Manus"是注册商标，建议尽快更改项目名称以避免法律问题，并提出可以通过去掉字母"M"来减少直接复制商标的可能性，同时保持一定的辨识度。
• [anxs] 作为项目发布者，详细介绍了LangManus的功能、技术架构及其开放源代码的社区驱动理念。强调了项目的多代理系统、工具集成以及易用性，并提供了演示视频和GitHub链接以供用户参与。
• [faizshah] 同意项目名称可能存在问题，建议可以采用"An Open Source alternative to X"的命名方式，同时指出许多类似项目依赖于浏览器使用。

补充讨论：
• [chris123] 提出了对教程的需求，希望有一个从Git克隆到成功运行的完整教程，帮助用户更好地理解和使用项目。
• [martypitt] 表示对项目中提示功能的赞赏，认为这是一个非常有用的资源。
• [sdrg822] 和 [rubenvanwyk] 对项目发布表示祝贺和赞赏。
• [stonexer] 简单表达了对项目的认可。

争议焦点：
• 项目名称是否侵犯商标权是讨论中的一个潜在争议点，[SweetSoftPillow] 和 [faizshah] 都提到了名称问题，并给出了各自的建议。

整体来看，讨论主要围绕项目的名称、功能实现以及用户需求展开，社区反馈积极且包含建设性意见。

Come From Open Source, Back to Open Source
LangManus is a community-driven AI automation framework that builds upon the incredible work of the open source community. Our goal is to combine language models with specialized tools for tasks like web search, crawling, and Python code execution, while giving back to the community that made this possible.
Demo
Task
: Calculate the influence index of DeepSeek R1 on HuggingFace. This index can be designed using a weighted sum of factors such as followers, downloads, and likes.
LangManus's Fully Automated Plan and Solution
:
Gather the latest information about "DeepSeek R1", "HuggingFace", and related topics through online searches.
Interact with a Chromium instance to visit the HuggingFace official website, search for "DeepSeek R1" and retrieve the latest data, including followers, likes, downloads, and other relevant metrics.
Find formulas for calculating model influence using search engines and web scraping.
Use Python to compute the influence index of DeepSeek R1 based on the collected data.
Present a comprehensive report to the user.

data.title: Quadlet: Running Podman containers under systemd
data.author: gjvc
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用Quadlet在systemd下运行Podman容器，替代已被弃用的`podman generate systemd`方法。Quadlet简化了将Podman容器作为systemd服务运行的过程，特别适用于需要在后台运行并希望在服务器重启后自动启动的容器。

过去的方法需要手动创建容器、生成systemd服务文件并进行配置，步骤繁琐且不易管理。而Quadlet通过在`~/.config/containers/systemd`目录中创建`.container`文件来定义容器配置，使用类似INI文件的格式，包含容器和systemd相关设置。这不仅简化了操作，还提供了更多灵活性，允许使用systemd的所有功能。

例如，创建一个PostgreSQL容器的配置文件`test-db.container`，可以指定镜像、自动更新、端口映射、卷和环境变量等。Quadlet使得Podman在功能和易用性上接近Docker Compose，同时更好地与systemd集成。

43456934.article_content:
Quadlet: Running Podman containers under systemd
2024-01-02
, updated: 2024-02-19
Tags:
#container
,
#linux
,
#selfhosting
Reading time: ~11min
Quadlet lets you run your Podman containers as systemd services.
This is especially useful for running containers in the background and automatically starting them after a server reboot.
Running Podman containers under systemd isn't new.
Indeed, this was supported by Podman for a long time with the command
podman generate systemd
.
But this command now shows a deprecation warning to migrate to Quadlet.
For some months, I was too lazy to do that migration on my home server.
Why even touch a working system?
But now that I finally found time for it, I really appreciate Quadlet!
I think that Podman finally has a Docker Compose alternative which is even more flexible and powerful!
In this blog post, I will explain how to use Quadlet with
rootless
Podman and migrate from the old method with
podman generate systemd
.
Note
If you wonder why systemd: Something has to start containers when there is no daemon (since Podman is daemonless).
If you are part of the vocal minority hating against systemd, then please leave instead of trolling.
Landscape mode recommended on mobile devices
Contents
The deprecated method
Let's see how the old method worked before comparing it to Quadlet.
You can skip to the Quadlet section though.
First, you had to create a container.
In an older post about
Containerized PostgreSQL with rootless Podman
, I created a container with a command similar to the following:
podman
create
\
--name
test-db
\
-p
5432:5432
\
-v
~
/volumes/test-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data:Z
\
-e
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME
\
--label
"io.containers.autoupdate=registry"
\
docker.io/library/postgres:16
The command details are explained in the older post.
The only option that isn't explained there is
--label "io.containers.autoupdate=registry"
.
This option enables updating the container image using
podman auto-update
which will be explained later in this post.
After creating the container, you can run the following command:
podman
generate systemd test-db
-fn --new
It creates the systemd service file
container-test-db.service
in your current path.
The options of the command aren't relevant for now, but they are also explained in the older post.
To use this generated service file, you had to place it in the directory
~/.config/systemd/user
.
To enable and start it, you had to run the following command:
systemctl
--user
enable
--now
container-test-db
The problem
The problem with the old method is that it required you to run commands to…
create a container
generate a service file
move the service file if not already in the mentioned directory
enable the service
Especially the command for creating the container is often lengthy.
This means that you had to create a shell script with these commands if you wanted to be able to rerun them later.
To reduce duplication, I created the following fish function to be called in my fish scripts that create the containers:
function
podman-default-create
set
-l
container_name $argv[
1
]
podman
create
\
--name
$container_name
\
--replace
\
$argv[
2
..
]
;
or return
1
podman
generate systemd
--no-header --new --name
$container_name
>~
/.config/systemd/user/container-$container_name.service
;
or return
1
systemctl
--user
enable
--now
container-$container_name
end
You don't have to understand the details of the function above.
What I want to demonstrate with it is that the old method was too hacky and involved the usage of redundant commands.
There must be an easier way, you might think.
Especially if you experienced the convenience that Docker Compose provides.
But this is not the only problem.
The old method is very inflexible!
If you want to cutomize the service file and use all systemd features, you need to
manually
edit it
after each generation
!
Quadlet
Let's take a look at the new method with Quadlet.
First, you create the directory
~/.config/containers/systemd
.
Then, you place a
.container
file inside it.
For example, here is the
test-db.container
file:
[Container]
Image
=
docker
.
io
/
library
/
postgres
:
16
AutoUpdate
=
registry
PublishPort
=
5432
:
5432
Volume
=
%h
/
volumes
/
test
-
db
:/
var
/
lib
/
postgresql
/
data
:
Z
Environment
=
POSTGRES_PASSWORD
=
CHANGE_ME
[Service]
Restart
=
always
[Install]
WantedBy
=
default
.
target
It is a normal systemd service file but with the special section
[Container]
.
This section has
many documented options
.
Almost all these options map to command line options that can be used to create a container with Podman (
podman create
).
The ones that we are interested in for the example are the following:
Image
specifies the image (with tag) to use
AutoUpdate=registry
maps to
--label "io.containers.autoupdate=registry"
(explained later in this post)
PublishPort
maps to
-p
Volume
maps to
-v
Environment
maps to
-e
It is important to use the
systemd specifier
%h
instead of
~
for the user home directory.

data.title: The Vatican's Latinist (2017)
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了美国神父雷吉纳尔德·福斯特（Reginald Foster）的独特经历。1970年，他因出色的拉丁文才被梵蒂冈相中，尽管其上级芬尼亚·莫纳汉（Finian Monahan）反对，他还是被带入梵蒂冈负责教宗的拉丁文信件。福斯特在梵蒂冈工作了四十年，以其直率个性和非传统言论闻名，如“我喜欢裸体做弥撒”等言论曾引发争议。尽管如此，他作为拉丁文教师的影响力巨大，被誉为“过去半个世纪最具影响力的拉丁文教师”，其教学方法独特且具变革性。福斯特强调拉丁文作为人类交流的媒介，而非仅供学术分析。他的教学风格严厉，反对学术虚饰，注重实际语言掌握。他的职业生涯虽有波折，但其对拉丁文教育的贡献深远。

43457202.article_content:
I
n
1970, the Procurator General of the Discalced Carmelite Order, Finian Monahan, was summoned to the Vatican for a meeting. The subject of the meeting was a promising young American priest by the name of Reginald Foster. The head Latinist of the Vatican’s State Department had tapped Foster to write papal correspondence, which was at the time composed entirely in Latin. Foster wanted the job but was bound by a vow of obedience, and the decision would be made by his superiors. Monahan intended to resist. Foster, thirty years of age, had proven himself to be both supremely intellectually gifted and utterly reliable—a precious thing at a time when the Catholic Church’s religious orders were hemorrhaging priests. Monahan thought Latin was a dead end. He didn’t want to lose one of his best to a Vatican department that would only get less and less important every year. He said Foster would go to the Vatican “over my dead body.”
Foster remembers the meeting vividly. “So we arrive there, and we’re ushered into this office, and who do we find there but Ioannes Benelli,” Foster says, using Benelli’s Latin name, as was customary at the Vatican at that time. He continues:
Benelli was Paul
VI
’s hatchet man—whenever he wanted something to get done, he called on Benelli. He was very energetic—got things done, and no nonsense. Everyone was terrified of him. I was too, and now here we were in the room with him, and he turns to Monahan and says, “This is Foster?” The General said yes. Then Benelli said, “Thank you very much, we won’t be needing you anymore.” And he took me by the hand and brought me down to the State Department and that was the end of that. Monahan didn’t say a word. I was now working for the Pope, and it was like I was more or less out of the Carmelite Order. A lot of the time the Order didn’t even really know what I was doing.
Foster would spend the next forty years at the Vatican, part of a small team of scribes who composed the pope’s correspondence, translated his encyclicals, and wrote copy for internal church documents. His somewhat unique position between the Carmelite Order and the Vatican bureaucracy meant that in fact he had a great deal of freedom for a priest. Later in his career his loose tongue—some in the church called it a loose cannon—would attract the notice of journalists looking for interesting copy. “Sacred language?” he said when asked about Latin as the “sacred language” of the church. “In the first century every prostitute in Rome spoke it fluently—and much better than most people in the Roman Curia.” The Minnesota
Star Tribune
quoted him as saying “I like to say mass in the nude,” which caused a small Curial kerfuffle (Foster claims he was misquoted). He appeared in Bill Maher’s movie
Religulous
, which featured him agreeing with the proposition that the Vatican itself was at odds with the message of Jesus, that the pope should not be living in a palace, and that hell and “that Old Catholic stuff” was “finished” and “gone.” Foster says the pope received complaints from bishops and cardinals about his appearance. “They said ‘Who is this Latinist of yours and what the hell is he doing?’ They would have fired me for sure. But by the time the film came out I was sick and a few months away from retirement anyway. So they just waited it out and let me go quietly.” He had already been fired from his post at the pontifical Gregorian University for allowing dozens of students to take his classes without paying for them.
B
es
ides being the Pope’s Latinist and “one of the Vatican’s most colorful characters” (as the Catholic News Service called him), Foster has been a tireless champion of Latin in the classroom. Indeed, Foster’s greatest legacy may be as a teacher. “The most influential Latin teacher in the last half-century is Reggie Foster,” says Dr. Nancy Llewellyn, professor of Latin at Wyoming Catholic College. “That’s not just my opinion—that’s a fact. For decades, he had the power to change lives like no other teacher in our field. I saw him for an hour in Rome in 1985 and that one hour completely changed my life. His approach was completely different from every other Latin teacher out there, and it was totally transformative.”
A humanist par excellence.
A humanist par excellence, Latin for Foster was not something to be dissected by linguistic analysis or serve as the raw data for a theory of gender or poetics: it was a language, a medium of human connection. I first met Foster in 1995, at his summer school, and couldn’t get enough: I returned seven times. No one on Earth was reading as much Latin as he and his students were, but he was more like an old-school newspaper editor than an academic: he wanted the
story
. But for that you actually had to know Latin, and know it well. Foster was ruthless about ignorance, and equally ruthless about anything that to him looked like mere academic posturing. “I don’t care about your garbage literary theory!” he barked at his students one day. “

data.title: Move on to ESM-Only
data.author: bpierre
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了JavaScript生态系统向ESM（ECMAScript Modules）单格式迁移的必要性和现状。作者在三年前主张双格式（CJS和ESM）并存以方便迁移，但随着工具和生态系统的演变，如今更倾向于ESM单格式。现代工具如Vite、Nuxt、SvelteKit等已原生支持ESM，简化了开发过程。

文章指出，尽管仍有大量CJS包，但ESM使用率在增长。采用ESM的主要挑战包括互操作性问题和依赖解析，但Node.js的新功能使得ESM包可以与CJS包无缝互操作。双格式维护复杂且容易出错，因此建议新包、浏览器包和独立CLI工具优先考虑ESM单格式。

作者认为，2025年将是ESM广泛采用的重要节点，建议包作者根据用户需求逐步迁移到ESM单格式。高层次框架和工具的支持将推动这一进程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ESM（ECMAScript Modules）与CJS（CommonJS）的现状、优缺点以及在不同环境下的应用情况

不同观点：
• **ESM已成熟，应全面转向ESM**：
   - **jauntywundrkind**：Node 20和22对ESM的支持已经完善，尤其是对仅ESM库的支持，因此不需要再使用CJS。
   - **bhouston**：过去两年只用ESM，体验非常好，尤其是在新项目中，非常自由和高效。
  
• **迁移到ESM存在实际困难**：
   - **patwolf**：在将遗留CJS项目迁移到ESM时遇到了`dd-trace`的bug，一年多未解决，表明迁移现有项目并非易事。
   - **jakub_g**：在大型TypeScript项目中迁移到ESM面临诸多问题，如需要修改文件扩展名，且工具支持不完善，导致编译时间过长。

• **工具和浏览器支持仍存在问题**：
   - **graypegg**：文章未提及浏览器对ESM的支持（如`<script type=“module”>`和importmaps），认为这是ESM支持的重要部分。
   - **codedokode**：尝试在浏览器中使用ESM时遇到问题，尤其是在没有web服务器和构建工具的情况下。
   - **shpx**：VS Code的扩展还不支持ESM，必须转译为CJS。

• **工具链和生态系统尚未完全支持ESM**：
   - **airstrike**：对"工具已准备好"的说法表示怀疑，认为尽管现代工具如Vite等支持ESM，但仍有许多配置和兼容性问题。
   - **darepublic**：不希望依赖复杂的bundler工具，希望能避免使用如Vite、Rollup等工具。

• **ESM在某些环境中的支持不足**：
   - **notanaverageman**：Goja（Go的JS运行时库）不支持ESM，导致需要将ESM包转换为CJS，且目前没有好的解决方案。

• **ESM的采用率存在争议**：
   - **sarreph**：对文章中ESM采用率的图表表示怀疑，认为ESM的增长趋势并不明显，可能还需要很多年才能广泛采用。

• **ESM在测试和调试中的问题**：
   - **plopz**：ESM在测试中面临mocking的问题，询问其他人如何解决。
   - **paulddraper**：在生产环境中，ESM的主要障碍是许多观测和追踪工具依赖CJS的`require()`。

补充讨论：
• **TypeScript与ESM的结合前景**：
   - **Klaster_1**：实验性的原生TS支持在Node.js中表现出色，认为可擦除语法是未来的方向，期待在浏览器中实现。

争议焦点：
• ESM是否已经完全准备好替代CJS，尤其是在现有项目迁移、工具支持和生态系统兼容性方面，仍存在较大争议。

43456966.article_content:
Move on to ESM-only
Feb 5
· 15min
The Toolings are Ready
Modern Tools
Top-Down & Bottom-Up
Requiring ESM in Node.js
The Troubles with Dual Formats
Interop Issues
Dependency Resolution
Package Size
When Should We Move to ESM-only?
New Packages
Browser-targeted Packages
Standalone CLI
Node.js Support
Know Your Consumers
How Far We Are?
Moving Forward
Three years ago, I wrote a post about
shipping ESM & CJS in a single package
, advocating for dual CJS/ESM formats to ease user migration and trying to make the best of both worlds. Back then, I didn’t fully agree with
aggressively shipping ESM-only
, as I considered the ecosystem wasn’t ready, especially since the push was mostly from low-level libraries. Over time, as tools and the ecosystem have evolved, my perspective has gradually shifted towards more and more on adopting ESM-only.
As of 2025, a decade has passed since ESM was first introduced in 2015. Modern tools and libraries have increasingly adopted ESM as the primary module format. According to
WOOORM
’s
script
, the packages that ships ESM on npm in 2021 was
7.8%
, and by the end of 2024, it had reached
25.8%
. Although a significant portion of packages still use CJS, the trend clearly shows a good shift towards ESM.
ESM adoption over time, generated by the
npm-esm-vs-cjs
script. Last updated at 2024-11-27
Here in this post, I’d like to share my thoughts on the current state of the ecosystem and why I believe it’s time to move on to ESM-only.
The Toolings are Ready
#
Modern Tools
#
With the rise of
Vite
as a popular modern frontend build tool, many meta-frameworks like
Nuxt
,
SvelteKit
,
Astro
,
SolidStart
,
Remix
,
Storybook
,
Redwood
, and many others are all built on top of Vite nowadays, that
treating ESM as a first-class citizen
.
As a complement, we have also testing library
Vitest
, which was designed for ESM from the day one with powerful module mocking capability and efficient fine-grain caching support.
CLI tools like
tsx
and
jiti
offer a seamless experience for running TypeScript and ESM code without requiring additional configuration. This simplifies the development process and reduces the overhead associated with setting up a project to use ESM.
Other tools, for example,
ESLint
, in the recent v9.0, introduced a new flat config system that enables native ESM support with
eslint.config.mjs
, even in CJS projects.
Top-Down & Bottom-Up
#
Back in 2021, when
SINDRESORHUS
first started migrating all his packages to ESM-only, for example,
find-up
and
execa
, it was a bold move. I consider this move as a
bottom-up
approach, as the packages that rather low-level and many their dependents are not ready for ESM yet. I was worried that this would force those dependents to stay on the old version of the packages, which might result in the ecosystem being fragmented. (As of today, I actually appreciate that move bringing us quite a lot of high-quality ESM packages, regardless that the process wasn’t super smooth).
It’s way easier for an ESM or Dual formats package to depend on CJS packages, but not the other way around. In terms of smooth adoption, I believe the
top-down
approach is more effective in pushing the ecosystem forward. With the support of high-level frameworks and tools from top-down, it’s no longer a significant obstacle to use ESM-only packages. The remaining challenges in terms of ESM adoption primarily lie with package authors needing to migrate and ship their code in ESM format.
Requiring ESM in Node.js
#
The
capability to
require()
ESM modules
in Node.js,
initiated
by
JOYEECHEUNG
, marks an
incredible milestone
. This feature allows packages to be published as ESM-only while still being consumable by CJS codebases with minimal modifications. It helps avoid the
async infection
(also known as
Red Functions
) introduced by dynamic
import()
ESM, which can be pretty hard, if not impossible in some cases, to migrate and adapt.
This feature was recently
unflagged
and
backported to Node.js v22
(
and soon v20
), which means it should be available to many developers already. Consider the
top-down or bottom-up
metaphor, this feature actually makes it possible to start ESM migration also from
middle-out
, as it allows import chains like
ESM → CJS → ESM → CJS
to work seamlessly.
To solve the interop issue between CJS and ESM in this case,
Node.js also introduced
a new
export { Foo as 'module.exports' }
syntax in ESM to export CJS-compatible exports (by
this PR
). This allows package authors to publish ESM-only packages while still supporting CJS consumers, without even introducing breaking changes (expcet for changing the required Node.js version).
For more details on the progress and discussions around this feature, keep track on
this issue
.
The Troubles with Dual Formats
#
While dual CJS/ESM packages have been a quite helpful transition mechanism, they come with their own set of challenges. Maintaining two separate formats can be cumbersome and error-prone, especially when dealing with complex

data.title: How arrow-rs is able to decode JSON so fast
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Arroyo团队如何通过arrow-rs库实现高效的列式JSON解码。JSON是流处理管道中常用的序列化格式，但其解析过程往往占用大量CPU资源。为了提高性能，Arroyo使用基于Apache Arrow的列式内存格式，并扩展arrow-json以支持流式处理、原始JSON存储和无效数据处理。通过批量解码，Arroyo能将JSON文档转换为列数组，实现高效操作。与Flink使用的Jackson反序列化器相比，arrow-json在处理大型嵌套记录时速度提升了2.3倍。文章详细介绍了列构建、字符串和列表处理以及结构解码等技术细节，展示了如何通过优化JSON解码提升流处理引擎的速度。
data.comments_summary:

43454238.article_content:
Blog
Updates from the Arroyo team
Fast columnar JSON decoding with arrow-rs
February 25, 2025
JSON is the most common serialization format used in streaming pipelines, so it pays to be able to deserialize it fast. This post covers in detail how the arrow-json library works to perform very efficient columnar JSON decoding, and the additions we've made for streaming use cases.
Micah Wylde
CEO of Arroyo
My day job is working on the
Arroyo
stream processing engine, which executes complex, stateful queries over
high-scale streams of events. Computing things like windowed aggregates, stream
joins, and incrementally-computed SQL involves, as you might imagine, a lot of
sophisticated algorithms and systems. Doing it much faster than existing systems
like Apache Flink took careful performance engineering at every level of the
stack.
But…I'm going to let you in on a little secret. The sad truth of this industry,
which no one will tell you, is that so, so many data pipelines spend the bulk of their
CPU time…deserializing JSON
1
.
That's right. Everybody's favorite human-readable and sorta-human-writable data
interchange format has been responsible for >50% of CPU usage on several
high-scale Flink pipelines I've worked on. And so if you want to build a
fast stream processing engine, you need to start with a fast JSON
deserialization strategy
2
.
Arroyo's internal data representation is built on top of
Arrow
, a columnar in-memory format designed for
fast analytical processing
3
. So our challenge is to take row-oriented JSON;
parse it, and build out columns from the corresponding field in each
document. And do this as fast as possible.
Fortunately, we don't have to start from scratch: the
arrow-rs project
includes a very fast JSON
decoder, largely written by
Raphael Taylor-Davies
. I found the approach quite
interesting and thought it was worth writing up. So we'll dig into how
arrow-json works and then talk through Arroyo's extensions to support
raw
JSON
—leaving parts of the JSON serialized—and the ability to skip records in a
batch that don't match the schema. Along the way you should pick up some
intuition for how to work with columnar data, which many engineers find
challenging and unfamiliar in our typically row-oriented world.
Table of contents
But is this fast?
Batched decoding
Stealing from the best
Run the tape

An example

Primitive and String decoding
Streaming extensions
Raw JSON

Wrapping up
But is this fast?
Before we get into the details, we might want to answer the question…is this
actually fast? And the answer is: yes! Benchmarking against the Jackson-based
deserializer used for Flink SQL, arrow-json is up to 2.3x faster:
Benchmark
Java (µs/record)
Rust (µs/record)
Speedup

(See
https://github.com/ArroyoSystems/json-benchmarks
for the benchmark source code and test documents.)
Arrow-json does particularly well with large, deeply nested records, and poorly
with enum-like structures where there are many null fields.
Batched decoding
Arrow, like other columnar formats, operates in
batches
. We're almost never
dealing with just one record (or “row”) of data, because columnar formats
achieve their high performance by storing many values together in a single
array. If you just have one row, the columnar overhead eats any performance
gains.
So our goal is to take a bunch of JSON documents (generally with a top-level
object) and turn them into a set of arrays representing each column of the
schema.
To make this concrete, let's take data representing HTTP server logs:

data.title: The HTML Review
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章展示了ASCII艺术和与之相关的一系列创作，包括文本和视觉元素。主画面是一个以ASCII码构成的卧室，伴随各种作者和作品名称，如Eileen Ahn的"Airs"和Reuben Son的"Pure Information"。文章探讨了幻觉、沟通、导航等主题，并通过不同的艺术形式表达。例如，Maya被描述为神和恶魔制造幻觉的超自然力量，而导航队列则比喻成没有终点的无限滚动条。其他作品如Nica Marimba和Answered Interruptions则通过音乐和中断的主题进行艺术表达。整体上，文章结合了视觉艺术和概念性探讨，呈现出多样化的数字创作。

主要讨论点：用户对UI设计的评价和其带来的感受

不同观点：
• [nhggfu] 认为UI设计非常出色，表达了对设计的赞赏，强调其卓越的视觉或交互体验。
• [mock-possum] 则从怀旧角度欣赏设计，特别提到了“old internet”的风格，并表示这种设计让他开始考虑是否需要一个平板设备来更好地享受这种艺术体验。这表明该用户更关注设计带来的情感共鸣和使用场景的延展。

补充讨论：
• [mock-possum] 的评论中提到了设计的怀旧元素，并进一步探讨了该设计对其个人设备选择的影响，这表明设计不仅在视觉上成功，还可能影响用户的消费决策。
• 虽然两个评论都对UI设计表示赞赏，但[mock-possum] 进一步延展了讨论，涉及到了设计在不同设备上的体验以及个人情感上的触动。

争议焦点：无明显争议，两个评论都对UI设计表示了正面评价，只是从不同角度出发。

data.title: A proof checker meant for education
data.author: alabhyajindal
data.article_summary: Deduce是一个自动化证明检查工具，旨在教育中帮助学生：1. 轻松入门，证明程序的正确性；2. 加深对逻辑的理解；3. 提高撰写数学证明的能力。该工具通过自动化验证帮助学生更好地掌握逻辑和证明技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Deduce软件的评价和相关问题的讨论

不同观点：
• [iNic] 认为Deduce的语法比Lean更友好，可能非常不错，但对Deduce的Live Code环境有抱怨，提到在运行代码时遇到`undefined variable: Nat`错误，导致体验不佳。
• [krick] 对Deduce是否适合作为教育工具表示疑问，不确定是否应该用Deduce而不是Lean进行学习，并指出学习Lean有95%在于学习其库。同时，krick表示自己没有实际使用过类似工具。
• [angelaguilera] 关注Deduce使用的软件许可证问题，提到虽然网站声称是开源的，但在GitHub仓库中未找到许可证信息。
• [ratmice] 表示喜欢教育性的证明检查器，认为Deduce的语法看起来不错，但指出缺少类似头文件的功能来声明证明类型。
• [rendaw] 质疑Deduce作为教育用途证明检查器的定位，反问为什么它不能作为通用证明检查器使用。
• [vitalmixofntrnt] 基于Curry-Howard同构，询问Deduce是否有编译器可以将证明编译成机器代码，并支持可选的内联汇编。
• [Q6T46nT668w6i3m] 对Deduce表示期待，提到喜欢并通常推荐Daniel Velleman的“Proof Designer”，但听说对初学者来说可能过于晦涩。

补充讨论：
• iNic的具体问题集中在Deduce的Live Code环境中的错误提示，影响了使用体验。
• krick对学习Lean和Deduce的取舍提出了自己的看法，尤其强调了Lean库的重要性。
• angelaguilera对开源许可证的关注显示了对软件法律和合规性的重视。
• ratmice从历史使用经验出发，对Deduce的功能提出了具体建议，并与其他工具进行了比较。
• rendaw对Deduce作为教育工具的定位提出质疑，但没有深入展开。
• vitalmixofntrnt的问题涉及高级技术实现，特别是Curry-Howard同构的应用。

Deduce is an automated proof checker meant for use in education to help students:
Ease their way into proving the correctness of programs.
Deepening their understanding of logic.
Improve their ability to write mathematical proofs.
43434503.article_summary: Deduce是一个自动化证明检查工具，旨在教育中帮助学生：1. 轻松入门，证明程序的正确性；2. 加深对逻辑的理解；3. 提高撰写数学证明的能力。该工具通过自动化验证帮助学生更好地掌握逻辑和证明技巧。
43434503.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Deduce软件的评价和相关问题的讨论

不同观点：
• [iNic] 认为Deduce的语法比Lean更友好，可能非常不错，但对Deduce的Live Code环境有抱怨，提到在运行代码时遇到`undefined variable: Nat`错误，导致体验不佳。
• [krick] 对Deduce是否适合作为教育工具表示疑问，不确定是否应该用Deduce而不是Lean进行学习，并指出学习Lean有95%在于学习其库。同时，krick表示自己没有实际使用过类似工具。
• [angelaguilera] 关注Deduce使用的软件许可证问题，提到虽然网站声称是开源的，但在GitHub仓库中未找到许可证信息。
• [ratmice] 表示喜欢教育性的证明检查器，认为Deduce的语法看起来不错，但指出缺少类似头文件的功能来声明证明类型。
• [rendaw] 质疑Deduce作为教育用途证明检查器的定位，反问为什么它不能作为通用证明检查器使用。
• [vitalmixofntrnt] 基于Curry-Howard同构，询问Deduce是否有编译器可以将证明编译成机器代码，并支持可选的内联汇编。

• ratmice从历史使用经验出发，对Deduce的功能提出了具体建议，并与其他工具进行了比较。
• rendaw对Deduce作为教育工具的定位提出质疑，但没有深入展开。
• vitalmixofntrnt的问题涉及高级技术实现，特别是Curry-Howard同构的应用。

data.title: The Mystery of the Oldest Writing System Remained Unsolved Until 1856
data.author: wyclif
data.article_summary: 在1850年代，楔形文字仍是未解之谜。直到四位学者竞相破译，这一世界上最古老的文字系统才开始揭示美索不达米亚古文明的秘密。特别是大英博物馆的一块有3000年历史的泥板，记录了亚述国王提格拉特帕拉沙尔一世的军事胜利。这块泥板成为破解楔形文字的关键，四位学者的竞争最终推动了古代文字的解读，揭开了历史的面纱。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对Hormuzd Rassam的身份认定及其背景的争议，以及对破译古文字方法的讨论]

不同观点：
• [yubblegum的观点] Hormuzd Rassam 不是阿拉伯人，而是亚述人。yubblegum 指出，Rassam 的名字 "Hormuzd" 源自古代伊朗对神明的称呼，因此不可能是阿拉伯人。此外，yubblegum 还提到，根据维基百科的资料，Rassam 的母亲来自犹太家庭，其祖父的名字是 Isaak Halabee，这是犹太名字 יצחק חליבה 的阿拉伯化变体。yubblegum 对史密森学会旗下的杂志出现这样的错误表示失望，尤其是在一篇讨论该地区古老语言的文章中。

• [对yubblegum观点的补充] yubblegum 引用了多个来源支持其观点，包括维基百科上关于 Hormuzd Rassam 的早期生活页面，以及关于 Ishak Haleva 的页面，指出 Haleva 和他祖父的名字相同，进一步证明 Rassam 的家庭背景具有犹太和亚述成分，而非阿拉伯背景。

• [z3t4的观点] z3t4 对破译古文字的方法提出疑问，询问是否通过猜测一个符号的意义，然后通过上下文推断其含义。同时，z3t4 提到了 "Rawlinson Method"（罗林森方法），但没有详细解释，暗示对这种破译方法的兴趣或疑惑。

补充讨论：
• yubblegum 对历史人物身份的细致考证反映了对历史和文化背景准确性的重视，尤其是在讨论古代语言和文化时。

• z3t4 的问题揭示了对古文字破译方法的兴趣，尤其是 "Rawlinson Method" 可能涉及的具体技术和步骤。这一问题可能引发进一步的讨论，关于破译古代文字的方法论及其在考古学中的应用。

争议焦点：Hormuzd Rassam 的民族身份是争议的核心，yubblegum 强调其亚述和犹太背景，而非阿拉伯背景，这与某些文献可能存在的错误认定形成对比。

data.title: Osgint – OSINT tool to find information about GitHub user
data.author: CHEF-KOCH
data.article_summary: OSGINT是一个开源工具，用于查找GitHub用户的各类信息。其主要功能包括：通过电子邮件查找GitHub用户名，通过用户名查找关联电子邮件（但并非每次都有效），以及获取用户资料信息（如账户创建日期、公开Gists、ID、公开PGP和SSH等）。该工具通过分析公开提交记录和GPG密钥来获取电子邮件信息，并利用GitHub的用户API进行数据检索。用户可以通过命令行指定用户名或电子邮件进行查询，并可以选择以JSON格式输出结果。工具还提供了示例输出，展示了查询结果的详细信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub 信息泄露及隐私问题，尤其是电子邮件地址的暴露，以及相关工具和用途的争议。

不同观点：
• **zellyn**：认为个人资料中的电子邮件信息可能不准确，提到有些邮件地址是他人提交代码时使用的。
• **Xaena**：指出该仓库的意图可能违反GitHub的可接受使用政策，特别是如果用于招聘或垃圾邮件目的，依据GitHub的隐私政策是可以举报的。
• **gokayburuc_dev**：质疑该功能是否必要，因为GitHub的API工具已经提供了类似的信息，并且大多数数据可以通过JSON格式免费获取。
• **cdblades**：认为有道德义务在README中加入如何避免信息泄露的说明，以保护用户隐私。
• **theyknowitsxmas**：质疑该工具的受益者，认为除了垃圾邮件发送者外，其他人不会从中受益。
• **1317**：认为该工具没有提供新的信息，除了电子邮件外，其他信息已经在GitHub的个人资料页面上公开。
• **ExxKA**：提到该工具可能为刚刚停止通过GitHub发送垃圾邮件的招聘人员提供了新的渠道。
• **cpursley**：指出该工具类似于https://reporeach.com，表明类似功能已经存在。
• **danso**：提供了技术上的建议，可以通过GitHub的Events API更高效地获取某人的最近提交和电子邮件信息。
• **Dotnaught**：认为这种方法比直接在提交后添加`.patch`要麻烦。
• **belter**：质疑谁会使用真实姓名注册GitHub，并给出了知名人物的例子（如Elon Musk和Donald Trump）。
• **areyourllySorry**：提到另一个类似工具“gitrecon”，表明类似功能和工具已经在开发者社区中存在。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于该工具是否会助长垃圾邮件行为，以及是否违反GitHub的隐私政策。
- 讨论中涉及了如何避免信息泄露以及保护个人隐私的技术和道德问题。
- 用户对于类似功能是否必要以及是否已有其他工具可以实现相同目的存在分歧。

data.title: The earliest versions of the first C compiler known to exist
data.author: diginova
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了由已故传奇人物dmr（Dennis M. Ritchie）编写的最早期的C语言编译器，这些编译器代码如今无法使用现代编译器如gcc进行编译。发布者仅为分享和缅怀这个点燃了万亿美金产业的火花。如果有人想尝试构建这个编译器，可以使用Aiju的PDP-11/Unix模拟器。同时提供了相关链接和资源，包括PDP-11模拟器和Research Unix资源库。代码主要由C语言（83.1%）和汇编语言（16.9%）编写。

data.title: Japanese scientists use stem cell treatment to restore movement in spinal injury
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 日本科学家通过使用诱导多能干细胞（iPS细胞）治疗脊髓损伤患者，取得初步成效。在Keio大学的研究中，四名患者中的两名在接受超过200万个iPS衍生神经细胞植入后，运动功能评分有所改善。其中一名老年男性患者已能站立并不借助支撑开始练习行走。研究主要目标是验证该疗法安全性，未观察到严重副作用。该研究获政府批准于2019年开始，首例手术在2022年进行。研究团队计划推进临床试验，以期将该疗法广泛应用于患者。

Japanese scientists use stem cell treatment to restore movement in spinal injury patients
Credit: Pixabay/CC0 Public Domain
A stem cell treatment helped improve the motor function of two out of four patients with a spinal cord injury in the first clinical study of its kind, Japanese scientists said.
There is currently no effective
treatment
for paralysis caused by serious spinal cord injuries, which affect more than 150,000 patients in Japan alone, with 5,000 new cases each year.
Researchers at Tokyo's Keio University are conducting their study using
induced pluripotent stem cells
(iPS)—created by stimulating mature, already specialized, cells back into a juvenile state.
They can then be prompted to mature into different kinds of cells, with the Keio researchers using iPS-derived cells of the neural stem.
The university said on Friday that the
motor function
score for two patients improved after an operation to implant more than two million iPS-derived cells into a spinal cord.
No serious adverse event was observed for all four cases after a year of monitoring, the university said.
The research's main goal was to study the safety of injecting the cells.
Public broadcaster NHK reported that one of the two was an elderly man who suffered the
injury
in an accident.
He is now able to stand without support and has started practicing walking, NHK said.
"We were able to achieve results in the world's first
spinal cord
treatment with iPS," Hideyuki Okano, a Keio professor who heads the research, said, according to NHK.
Okano said the team hoped to move to a clinical trial that would be a step towards bringing the treatment to patients.
The university received
government approval
for their initial study in 2019 and they carried out the first operation in 2022.
Details of the patients remain confidential, but the team is focusing on people who were injured 14-28 days before the operation.
The number of cells implanted was determined after safety experiments in animals.
